subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should ordinary Discord routed replies support a binding or per-agent visible identity override, and should that be implemented through webhook persona delivery, bot self-profile mutation, or deferred?
rationale: This creates a new public Discord identity surface backed by bot or webhook credentials, so automation should not choose the API shape, auth boundary, fallback behavior, or cross-channel semantics.

options.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
options.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path that reuses webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit credential storage, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Coordinate with self-profile
options.body: Treat nickname/avatar mutation as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 and only add it after the self-only action gate and guild/channel semantics are approved.

options.title: Defer per-binding identity
options.body: Keep current bot-account replies plus thread-bound webhook persona behavior and ask users to use multiple bot accounts or approved thread-bound flows for now.

recommendation.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
recommendation.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path that reuses webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit credential storage, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged webhook/persona delivery path and can judge whether it should become ordinary routed-reply behavior.
